read_by: Agent-drafted, from the cell's own tier table and decision log
input: Water depth above the first floor (ft), -4 to 24 ft (retail coastal curve -1 to 10 ft); depth above ground is accepted with the building's floor height
out_of_scope: Contents (declared as a withheld placeholder part)
missing_mechanisms: Waves and fast-moving water (wave and velocity zones)

how_to_use.share_of: Structure replacement cost new of the same building (no land, contents or depreciation)

outputs.single_event: conditional: proposal, not in the runtime index; the request must name the building and the water type
outputs.scenario_dollars: withheld until the building value is qualified
outputs.yearly_loss: withheld before promotion (computed by the consumer afterwards)

conditions: flood_water_type is required; unknown water withholds
When Hazard sends depth above the floor it must apply the dry-ground rule itself (depth above ground of 0 or less means no damage)

method.summary: FEMA Hazus depth-damage functions used as published, one per building (house DF 129, warehouse DF 341, office DF 431, each for river and coastal still water); retail keeps Hazus DF 217 for river water and USACE NACCS for coastal surge

key_sources: FEMA, Hazus Flood Model Technical Manual 7.0 (2025), Table 5-2 (FRE-S002)
USACE, North Atlantic Coast Comprehensive Study (2015), depth-damage functions (FRE-S004)
FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP redacted claims, v3 (FRE-S012; check only)
judgment: No value per area set, so scenario dollars stay withheld
No adjustment for the gap between river and coastal claims (coastal commercial claims run higher)

checks.name: NFIP flood-insurance claims by depth band (about 105,000 claims)

open_items: Office curve reads about 1.6 times the claims for 3+ storey buildings (kept as published)
Wave and velocity zones not modelled
Contents placeholder: keep or drop (for the reviewer)
